question: The first industrial policy of Government of India was announced in _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1948**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first industrial policy** of independent India was announced on **6 April 1948**. It laid the foundation for the country's industrial development.
 
• The policy emphasized a **mixed economy model**, where both the public and private sectors would play significant roles in industrial development.
 
• The 1948 Industrial Policy Resolution categorized industries into **four groups** based on their ownership and control: those exclusively under the state, those progressively under state control, those in the public-private partnership, and those left to private enterprise.
 
• The government also emphasized the importance of **small-scale industries** as a means of employment generation and self-reliance.
 
• This policy marked the beginning of India's journey towards planned economic development and industrialization post-independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy of 1948:**

 
 
• The policy served as a **blueprint** for India's industrial growth and aimed to reduce dependence on imported goods by encouraging domestic production.
 
• It also highlighted the necessity for **state intervention** in essential industries, such as defense, infrastructure, and energy, to ensure national security and economic stability.
 
• The policy outlined the need for **labor welfare**, social justice, and equitable distribution of wealth.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Industrial Policies:**
 
 
• Following the 1948 policy, India introduced the **Industrial Policy of 1956**, which emphasized the development of a socialistic pattern of society and gave the public sector a commanding role.
 
• The **Industrial Policy of 1991** marked a significant shift towards liberalization, privatization, and globalization, reducing the state's role in industrial activities.
 
 
 
• **Mixed Economy Model:**
 
 
• India adopted a mixed economy model under the 1948 policy, balancing the roles of both private and public sectors in economic activities.
 
• This model aimed to combine the **efficiency of private enterprises** with the **social objectives** of the public sector.
 
 
 
• **Small-Scale Industries:**
 
 
• The 1948 policy recognized the importance of small-scale industries in generating **employment** and promoting **self-reliance** in rural areas.
 
• Special incentives and support were provided to promote these industries, including financial assistance and training programs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the 1948 Policy:**

 
 
• It marked the beginning of a systematic approach to industrial development in India.
 
• It addressed issues like **capital formation, labor welfare, and equitable resource distribution**.
 
 
 
• **Public and Private Sector Roles:**
 
 
• The public sector was assigned the responsibility for industries critical to national security and economic stability.
 
• The private sector was encouraged to invest in less critical industries to promote entrepreneurship and innovation.
